VISITE // BOULANGERIE D'ÉTAT N° 12, RU: VISIT  //  STATE BAKERY NO. 12, MILL STREET
Cliquez sur un endroit du dessin pour l': Click a spot on the drawing to examine it. What you find is added to the file.
Sept heures. La file d'attente commence:
Seven o'clock. The queue starts at the corner of Mill Street. When you walk past everyone with your card, conversations stop.

Zora KOVAC wipes her hands on her apron. "You've come about the coupons. Go ahead. I have nothing to hide, and no time."

You have time to look at four things.
Derrière les sacs de papier, un cahier d: Behind the paper bags, a school exercise book. Since 15 September Zora has been noting the customers she does not know: twenty-three names, all with new ration books, all on Thursdays. "I wanted to be believed."
Les tickets du jour sont classés par car: Today's coupons are sorted by book, with an accountant's rigour. One stub catches your eye: book no. 4-1187, HORVAT Milan, block 3, flat 12. Cashed on 16 October.
Vous sortez. Une vieille femme vous parl: You step outside. An old woman speaks to you without looking at you, the way one speaks to the pavement: "They're the cemetery books. A little man with glasses, from the Bureau. He sells them on Thursdays at the covered market. Everyone knows. Nobody will tell you twice."
Des sacs de farine, un four encore chaud: Sacks of flour, an oven still warm. Under a tea towel, two loaves set aside, with a label: "Brezno". Zora does not lower her eyes. "My sister. She has three children. Arrest me for that if you like."
Accroché à un clou, le cahier des contrô: Hanging from a nail, the inspection book. On 18 September, the inspector wrote "Nothing to report" and signed. Below, in another hand: "Reported unknown customers. Answer: not your job. Z. K."
Une lettre de Tomas, de la caserne. Il d: A letter from Tomas, at the barracks. He asks for socks and says the food is good. Zora takes it back from your hands, in front of the whole queue watching through the window. She says nothing. The neighbourhood will remember.
Quand vous ressortez, la file s'écarte p: When you come back out, the queue parts to let you through. Nobody looks at you, and everybody has seen you.
